heroSubtitle: Nine tourism regions, twenty-five provinces, and curated corridors — with verified place details, maps, and trusted local contacts.
whyIntro: We are not reselling somebody else's database. Every region, province and place on this site was visited, written up and photographed by people who live and travel here.

why.title: Checked on the ground
why.body: Every site, stay and kitchen is visited before it goes on the map, then looked at again each season. If a place closes, it comes off.

why.title: Details that hold up at the gate
why.body: Entry fees, opening hours, ticket rules and road conditions written as you will actually find them — not copied from a brochure.

why.title: Maps that work offline
why.body: Every province, corridor and site is mapped, so the route still opens when the signal drops somewhere past Sen Monorom.

why.title: Trusted local contacts
why.body: Guides, boat owners and homestay families we have met in person, with numbers that get answered in Khmer or English.

testimonials.name: Sophea Chan
testimonials.text: The listing warned that the Preah Vihear access road turns to mud after heavy rain and gave a number for a driver who does it anyway. Both turned out to be exactly right.

testimonials.name: Marta Nowak
testimonials.text: We planned four provinces in ten days off this site alone. Ferry times to Koh Rong Sanloem were correct to the minute, which is not something I expected.

testimonials.name: Daniel Okoye
testimonials.text: Saved a dozen places before we flew, then had the whole Mondulkiri list offline when the signal went. The Bunong homestay was the best night of the trip.
